ordered_diagnoses: Multifocal Eosinophilic Granuloma with Central Diabetes Insipidus

s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic multisystem disorder with skin manifestations and endocrine abnormalities
salient_findings: Numerous asymptomatic reddish-brownish papules, nodules, and plaques over the whole body
Central diabetes insipidus, growth retardation, and hypothyroidism
key_facts: 7-year medical history of skin lesions
Skin lesions began on bilateral eyelid margins and extended to trunk and extremities
Patient has central diabetes insipidus
Patient has growth retardation
Patient has hypothyroidism
Skin biopsy showed dense granulomatous infiltrate in the upper dermis
Immunohistochemical results were negative for CD1a and S-100, positive for CD68

Skin lesions are present on periocular areas, perioral areas, neck, shoulder, axillary folds, cubital fossa, wrists, palms, umbilical region, lateral abdomen, inguinal area, anogenital area, popliteal fossa, and ankles

shortlist: Multifocal Eosinophilic Granuloma with Central Diabetes Insipidus

shortlist.label: Erdheim-Chester Disease
shortlist.why_kept: Matches chronic multisystem disorder with skin manifestations and endocrine abnormalities, and specific histiocytic infiltration pattern

shortlist.label: Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis
shortlist.why_kept: Consistent with skin lesions, diabetes insipidus, and growth retardation, despite negative CD1a and S-100 immunohistochemical results

shortlist.label: Multifocal Eosinophilic Granuloma with Central Diabetes Insipidus
shortlist.why_kept: Aligns with patient's central diabetes insipidus, skin lesions, and histiocytic infiltration

shortlist.label: Necrobiotic Xanthogranuloma
shortlist.why_kept: Possible given the patient's skin lesions and presence of granulomatous infiltrate, although less typical for endocrine abnormalities

shortlist.label: Sarcoidosis with Endocrine Abnormalities
shortlist.why_kept: Could explain the multisystem disorder, skin manifestations, and endocrine abnormalities, despite less specific histiocytic pattern

raw.rationale: The patient's 7-year medical history of numerous asymptomatic reddish-brownish papules, nodules, and plaques, along with the presence of central diabetes insipidus, growth retardation, and hypothyroidism, are consistent with Erdheim-Chester Disease. The skin biopsy findings of a dense granulomatous infiltrate in the upper dermis with negative CD1a and S-100 and positive CD68 immunohistochemical results also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis
rejected.why: Negative CD1a and S-100 immunohistochemical results do not support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Multifocal Eosinophilic Granuloma with Central Diabetes Insipidus
rejected.why: While the patient has central diabetes insipidus, the skin lesions and biopsy findings are more consistent with Erdheim-Chester Disease.

rejected.label: Necrobiotic Xanthogranuloma
rejected.why: The clinical presentation and biopsy findings do not match those typically seen in Necrobiotic Xanthogranuloma.

rejected.label: Sarcoidosis with Endocrine Abnormalities
rejected.why: While sarcoidosis can cause granulomatous inflammation, the specific combination of clinical and biopsy findings in this case is more consistent with Erdheim-Chester Disease.
